is found to lead them except that God willed to come into flesh, and those who persevere have no other hope than that the circuit [?] of the world, that is, the land of faithlessness, be conquered. Then, when the shoe of the Lord's feet, that is, the gospel of peace, has been shown, Dagon, the work of the world, is destroyed, and when the ark of the covenant, which we are, has been released, the speech of the Philistines urging alien things is overcome. So whoever has learned the things that are set in regions, spoken of places and foretold of kings should conquer by disciplined effort the places, kingdoms and regions of the vices within himself; and though he understands that it was prophesied of God, he should still recognize that it is set before him as a kind of pattern for life. For from beginning to end, as we come into this world, just as we are deceived by the joined ways of wickedness, so we are saved by joined faith and correction.
PRISCILLIAN'S BLESSING OVER THE FAITHFUL

Holy Father, almighty God, who, forming the temple of your manifold grace and the tabernacle of the Church ordered in you, and stretching out the measures of immeasurable glory, taught us with Christ as author in you that in you alone, by the working of the Holy Spirit, there should be brought about both the fullness of invisibility, which the Father owed to the Son, and the visibility of acknowledgment, which the Son owed to the Father. So you set in yourself the boundary of every defined thing and the receptacle of things without limit, so that to us who come from you alone you might open one way forth, and to us who return to you one entrance into the rising of the Son who rises in you. And though people made their way to your tabernacle by different paths of calling, all would still enter to you by the one entrance of Christ at work, so that whoever found him shut would have no access to you, because he had not known the Father of the Son in the Son and the Son of the Father in the Father. For you are God, who, being in all the origins of powers, within and without, surpassing

and inward, surrounding and poured into all things, are believed to be one God; you are found invisible in the Father, visible in the Son, and, united for the work of both, the Holy Spirit. For you are your own author of what you are, and you show nothing outside yourself that could seem more excellent than you. And though our mind, attempting the work of an understanding that cannot be unfolded, is shut in by the error of human weakness, it still grasps from the voices of the prophets the one way of devout belief about you: that we know you as one God in all things in such a way that we hold no place, either of what is made or of what works, to be not in you, nor any to be outside you. And so, as you possess and are possessed, you are found neither outside the whole in any one thing, nor absent from all things. For in you and through you lies the whole ordering of all that comes forth: you are father to souls, brother to sons, son to brothers, friend to the elect, neighbour to those who draw near, the working of spirits,

the source of archangels, the work of angels; you are the whole empowering of powers. Through you the works of all things were ordered. You marked off the parts of each thing, and, joining the elements to one another, you set the bounds of a well-ordered work, giving them the spirit of life, so that, though of themselves they could do nothing, yet, animated by the greatness of the one who works in them, they might fulfil the ministry of the service bound to them by you. And after this, looking upon the earth, you brought forth the living soul. Though it was not from itself, yet, so that the word of command should not be empty, where your command was the beginning of things that did not exist, the earth, quickened by the command, brought forth what it did not itself possess. And your command became the nature of things that could appear, so that, as it brought forth its work from nothing, things first appeared unformed and darkened; afterwards you gave feeling to the unfeeling, sight to the darkened, smell to the brute, sound to the hard and hearing to the hardened,

so that, with you present everywhere, the word might arrange for the use of your work the matter of things which the command had brought forth without form; and, calling each thing by its name, raising up the lofty, sloping the inclined, filling the hollows, opening the plains, covering the hidden depths of the forests, it might make the whole glory of created things sing together to you alone, for the acknowledgment of your knowledge. And though mute things could not confess you in speech, reason, speaking through the ordering of things, would not withhold its testimony to your omnipotence. [?] ... What exchange worthy of you shall we give for our souls, holy Father, almighty God? Or what is man, that you are mindful of him, or the son of man, that you visit him, except that, for the glory of so great a work brought forth, we recognize that we are your handiwork in the good works which you prepared, that we should walk in them? And so our mind and our speech speak of you, because, made indestructible through you, where [?] ...
